newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia pledges to pay army debts in July-August.
newsitem.headline: Russia pledges to pay army debts in July-August.

text.p: Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin said on Monday he had been instructed by President Boris Yeltsin to repay all debts to the armed forces in July and August, Itar-Tass news agency said.
Speaking to military academies graduates in the Kremlin, Chernomyrdin said he had a telephone conversation with Yeltsin earlier on Monday.
He did not say what the size of the debt was, nor where the money was coming from.
Military officials say the debt, including wages to officers and funds for army maintainance, amounts to trillions, if not tens of trillions of roubles (several billion dollars).
The government said last week it had repaid all pension arrears, meeting the July 1 deadline set by Yeltsin earlier this year.
During his re-election campaign last summer, Yeltsin ordered Russia's 1.8-million-strong conscript army to transform itself into a smaller professional battle-ready force by the year 2000.
Chernomyrdin reiterated on Monday that the armed forces had to be reformed urgently, taking into account the country's economy.
"Delays are inadmissible. Every day costs us," Tass quoted him as saying.
"The military reform is aimed at making the armed forces compact and mobile, but efficient and equipped with the most modern armaments and technical means."
